messages.subject: html.Index and RenderUI.
parts:
Hello Everybody,
I am having a little problem (quite annoying in fact) with renderUI. I usually manage to find a solution by searching through stackoverflow and this group, but this time no luck.

So for different reasons, I am building my UI entirely in html using an index.html file.
I am trying to populate a <div> with renderUI, with no luck.

in my index.html 
<div id="summary" class="shiny-html-output shiny-bound-output"></div>

and in my UI 
output$summary <- renderUI({
   ##pulling stuff here
    HTML(paste0('<h4><u>Some HTML here </h4></u>')
    ))
  
})

So am trying to understand how those two interact, and why in that case it is not rendering anything. I know the syntax of the renderUI is correct, because it's rendering properly in a test app, that doesn't have an index.html but an ol' good ui.R. If anybody could help me, that would be greatly appreciated !

thank you.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: html.Index and RenderUI.
parts:
Remove shiny-bound-output from the div class and I think it should work. shiny-bound-output is added at runtime by Shiny itself so it can keep track of what elements it has already seen.

In general, you should determine the HTML for a UI component simply by executing it at the R console (rather than by using your web browser's inspector tools):

> uiOutput("summary")
<div id="summary" class="shiny-html-output"></div>

Thank you Joe, 
it was pretty stupid from my part. I usually run in the R console to get the proper html code.

I now have another styling problem, still with that <div>. The actual <div id = summary> thinks he has a height of 0 and push all the elements after, because there is something in it. The actual elements populated inside that <div> knows their correct height on the other hand. Since it's reactive and the content will change, specifying a height wouldn't solve the issue. It's like the html page create the div, with a height of zero, and then doesn't know that there is elements inside him that shiny have populated.

Any ideas on what could cause that issue ?
